reviews.one_line_contribution: A crossover estimand for agentic memory: at one fixed GEPA-optimized instruction, on the same test instances, compare the gain from the bank distilled from the episodes that instruction was optimized on ('own', cells 6 and 10) against the bank from episodes it never saw ('other', cells 7 and 9), so that the well-documented shrinkage of memory's gain at a better prompt can be split into headroom (any better prompt leaves less room) versus genuine information-specific absorption by the instruction container (S_info). The crossover is the new thing; the substitution framing and the compile-once prediction are not.
reviews.closest_prior_work: EvoAgentBench (arXiv 2607.05202), which the proposal itself concedes: Memento, ReasoningBank and GEPA on a shared 528/267 trajectory split, three backbones, four domains. It threatens the framing (the 'nobody has put a retriever and an optimizer on the same trajectories' sentence is already withdrawn) but not the estimand, because a side-by-side table cannot separate headroom from absorption without the own/other contrast. The residual novelty therefore rests entirely on an absence claim about EvoAgentBench's contents that the proposal admits it could not verify (PDF unopened, arXiv unreachable). Second: MIPROv2 (arXiv 2406.11695), whose instruction-only vs demonstration-only vs joint ablation on one training set is the two-container question for static demonstrations; it does not hold episodes out across containers, which is exactly the crossover's contribution, but a reviewer will compress Delta_info to 'the MIPROv2 ablation plus a train/train split with retrieval', and that compression is not unfair. Third: Experience Distillation (arXiv 2607.21051) already owns the retention-ratio shape with weights as the second container; swapping weights for an instruction is a cheaper and more deployable container but not a conceptually new measurement.
reviews.strongest_objection: The primary success criterion is a ratio the design is not powered for, and the quantity it IS powered for is not the quantity the title claims. Note that Delta_info algebraically reduces to acc(I1a x M_b) - acc(I1a x M_a): the acc(I x M0) term cancels, so the well-powered contrast (SE ~0.7pt, MDE ~2pt) is a bare provenance comparison between two banks at one instruction, which by itself licenses only 'a bank whose episodes the optimizer saw helps less than one it did not' - not 'most of memory's gain is substitutable'. The substitution claim lives in S_info = 1 - own/other, whose denominator reintroduces the M0 cells (5 and 8) and their noise. Run the proposal's own central scenario: G1 clears at g(I0,B_a) = 7pt, S_raw ~0.7 so own = g(I1a,B_a) ~ 2pt, headroom share at the predicted midpoint of 50% so other = g(I1a,B_b) ~ 4.5pt. Then Delta_info = 2.5pt, already below the pre-registered 3pt claim threshold, and S_info = 0.56 with SE ~0.20 by the delta method using the proposal's own SE(Delta_info)=0.7pt and SE(other)~1.0pt, giving a 90% CI of roughly [0.23, 0.89] - knife-edge against the required exclusion of 0.2, and failing outright if the gate clears at 6pt instead of 7, or if the headroom share lands at 60% instead of 50%, both of which are inside the proposal's own predicted 30-70% band. Prediction 1 thus fails under the proposal's median expected parameters, and the pre-registered fallback ('if mean(other) < 3pt, S_info is undefined') makes an uninterpretable primary the modal outcome. The Measurement section computes an MDE for Delta_info and for S_raw but never for S_info, which is the binding criterion. A second, cheaper failure mode compounds it: prediction 1 also demands direction consistency in both crossover directions, but G6 tolerates a 3pt bank-quality imbalance measured on S_dev n=300, where the SE of that imbalance estimate is ~3.4pt - the gate has essentially no power. A constant 2pt quality gap between B_a and B_b cancels in the two-direction mean (which is why the crossover is run both ways) but splits a true 2.5pt effect into ~0.5pt and ~4.5pt, so the both-directions requirement fails while the estimand is fine. Secondarily, and more likely to be voiced out loud in review: this audits the ExpeL/ReasoningBank evaluation template in a regime those papers never claimed, on 27-32B open-weight agents where the program's own prior study found the ExpeL bank TOST-equivalent to no memory (+0.6pt), after screening four agent x format pairings to find one where memory does anything at all, with the only larger-scale cell (gpt-oss-120b, cell 25) pre-declared 'never load-bearing' and Risk 11 refusing to reproduce any target's own setting.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: 1) Fix the estimand/power mismatch before freezing: either pre-register Delta_info as the sole confirmatory endpoint with S_info demoted to descriptive-with-CI, or power the ratio explicitly - report the analytic SE(S_info) as a function of the observed 'other' gain, and pre-register a gain-conditional threshold instead of a flat 'CI excludes 0.2'. If the ratio is demoted, cells 5 and 8 (8,000 episodes) stop being load-bearing for the primary and that budget can go into more optimizer seeds on cells 6/7/9/10, which is where the SE actually lives. 2) Replace the both-directions consistency requirement with a fitted direction x half interaction term, and measure bank balance on S_test n=1000 rather than a 3pt tolerance at S_dev n=300 where the SE of the imbalance is larger than the tolerance. 3) Add the full-data arms (see missing_baseline) so the paper says something about a system a practitioner could build. 4) Add a re-distilled B_a: same half-a episodes, different distiller model or an enforced paraphrase, so surface/textual redundancy with I1a is broken while episode provenance is held. Without it, 'own helps less' is equally explained by token redundancy between an instruction and a bank written from the same episodes by the same frontier distiller, which is not information absorption in the sense the title asserts. 5) Add a procedural positive control alongside B_a+dup10. Near-duplicate test questions with the same answers are non-substitutable by construction - no instruction can compress 100 specific answers - so prediction 6 is close to guaranteed and certifies only that the logging and pairing work, not that the instrument can distinguish absorbed from unabsorbed *procedural* value, which is the only kind at issue. A control that injects a genuinely procedural, instance-specific rule (e.g. a per-entity disambiguation step) would test the thing that matters. 6) Open the EvoAgentBench PDF before the design freeze rather than after; the entire novelty delta is an absence claim about its tables.
reviews.missing_baseline: The full-training-set head-to-head: I1_{a+b} x M0, I0 x M_{a+b}, and I1_{a+b} x M_{a+b} on all 800 training episodes. Every number in the grid - S_raw, S_info, the compile recommendation - is computed at 400 episodes per container because the halving is an identification device, and cell 18's 'recommended deployment' (I1b x C_a) pairs an instruction optimized on half b with a block compiled from half a, a configuration no practitioner would ever build. A reviewer will ask the obvious operational question - given my whole training set, should I optimize the prompt, build the bank, or both - and the plan as written cannot answer it, while the title and abstract clearly imply it can. Secondary omission: no bank distilled from half a by a different distiller (the re-distillation control above), so episode provenance and textual redundancy with I1a are never separated.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is well above the usual standard for a proposal: a dated scan (2026-09-03, prior 2026-08-21), 15 enumerated queries, 54 by-id verifications, committed scan records, a stated two-channel drop rule, and an explicit correction retracting v2's false negatives on five IDs. Credit for treating a failed search as a search failure rather than as evidence of absence. Two things nevertheless make it a weakness rather than a neutral. First, the check cannot support the claim it is being asked to support. arXiv is unreachable from the node and EvoAgentBench's PDF (2607.05202) was never opened, so the entire novelty delta - 'no combined optimizer-plus-memory cell, no token matching, no compiled-bank arm, no paired statistics' - rests on an abstract, a project page method list, and search-surfaced descriptions of Table 3. Combined cells and token-matched ablations are precisely the things that live in appendices and never appear in abstracts, so the search method is structurally blind to the one collision that would matter. The proposal's own stated residual risk ('a GEPA + memory ablation may exist in an appendix of a systems paper') names exactly the failure its procedure cannot detect. Second, the check already concedes that several non-primary claims are pre-empted in direction: compile-beats-or-matches-retrieve by arXiv 2608.14036 (skills > Workflow Memory by 6.06pt) and 2606.30775 (single rewrite ~ iterative refinement), which makes prediction 4 and secondary endpoint (a) confirmatory rather than novel, and Experience Distillation (2607.21051) already publishes the retention-ratio shape. I can independently verify only the pre-2026 anchors (ExpeL 2308.10144, ReasoningBank 2509.25140, Memp 2508.06433, A-MEM 2502.12110, GEPA 2507.19457, MIPROv2 2406.11695); every 2026 ID here is beyond what I can check, so the absence claims must be taken on trust from a channel the author has already flagged as insufficient. Verdict: no collision I can name kills the crossover estimand, but the proposal has not established that one does not exist, and it says so itself.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A crossover identification design that separates 'memory's gain shrinks because the prompt got better' from 'memory's gain shrinks because the instruction already absorbed that specific information': two disjoint training halves each produce a bank and a GEPA-optimized instruction, and at a fixed instruction on fixed test instances the own-half bank (cells 6, 10) is compared against the other-half bank (cells 7, 9), so headroom and instruction identity are identical by construction and the own-vs-other difference Delta_info is attributable to shared training-episode information rather than to prompt quality.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two, at different distances. (a) MIPROv2 (2406.11695) is the framing precedent a reviewer names first: it factorizes a prompt into instructions and bootstrapped demonstrations and ablates instruction-only vs demonstration-only on one training set, which is literally the two-container question. It does not threaten the core: its demonstrations are statically selected, not query-conditioned retrieval, it never holds episodes out across containers, and it reports no residual ratio, so it cannot produce Delta_info. (b) EvoAgentBench (2607.05202) is the real threat: it already places ReasoningBank/Memento retrievers and GEPA on identical training trajectories across four domains and three backbones, which kills the 'nobody has put these in one table' framing (correctly withdrawn here) and pre-empts the motivation. The proposal's remaining delta rests entirely on the assertion that EvoAgentBench has no combined optimizer-plus-memory cell, no token matching and no paired statistics -- an absence claim the authors admit they could not verify against the PDF. If any EvoAgentBench cell or appendix runs GEPA-instruction-plus-retrieved-bank, cells 5-10 become a seed-and-split refinement of a published table rather than a new result. The nearest measurement-object precedent, Experience Distillation (2607.21051, 'retains >=64.8% of the in-context gain'), already establishes the retention-ratio shape with weights as the second container; substituting an instruction for weights is an incremental move on that axis.
reviews.strongest_objection: The primary endpoint is very likely to be undefined or unreachable under the proposal's own pre-registered rules, and nothing in the gate structure prevents that. Prediction 1 demands Delta_info >= 3pt AND S_info >= 0.5 with the 90% CI excluding 0.2; since S_info = 1 - own/other, satisfying both requires mean(other) >= 6pt and mean(own) <= 3pt -- i.e. a held-out-half bank must still deliver a six-point gain on top of a GEPA-optimized instruction. But G1 gates the bank effect at I0 (>=6pt paired, lower 80% CI >=3pt), not at I1, and every result the proposal itself cites predicts the I1-side number will be far smaller: the program's own pilot found the ExpeL bank TOST-equivalent to zero on Qwen3.5-27B (+0.6pt, 90% CI [-1.2, +2.5]) and a one-line instruction dominating every memory manipulation; EvoMemBench, MemHarness (70.1 vs 76.4 on ALFWorld) and the headroom logic all point the same way. The modal outcome is therefore g(I1a, B_b) in the 1-4pt band, where the proposal's own branch says S_info is 'undefined and Delta_info alone is reported' and where the pre-registered 3pt claim threshold sits at or above the effect itself. The paper then consists of outcome (i) -- 'the drop is headroom, the un-optimized-prompt framing is withdrawn' -- which is the authors' own stated most-likely death, plus a descriptive retrieval/compile/dump ladder. That is an honest null, but a reviewer will ask what the ICLR contribution is when the identification arm the whole design is built around returns 'inconclusive', and will note that the design bought a 44,000-episode primary grid to answer a question it gated in the wrong place. Compounding this: SE(Delta_info) ~= 0.7pt is optimistic, because all eight contrasts (4 seeds x 2 directions) run on the same 1000 instances, so instance-level discordance (which the proposal's own arithmetic puts at ~1.1-1.3pt for a single contrast) does not average down by sqrt(8) under a cluster bootstrap that resamples instances.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Four concrete changes, roughly in order of importance. (1) Move the gate to where the endpoint lives: add a pre-registered S_dev gate requiring g(I1a(s), B_b) -- memory gain at an already-optimized instruction from a bank the optimizer never saw -- to clear roughly 6pt, not just G1's 6pt at I0. If that fails on S_dev, the study should be re-framed before S_test is touched as the headroom paper (the honest and still-publishable version: 'a memory bank's headline delta is measured at a prompt with headroom, and here is exactly how much of it survives an optimizer'), with the ladder and coupling cells as the body, rather than discovering that after 44,000 episodes. (2) Add the union-half instruction I1_{a+b} as a Tier 0 cell (see missing_baseline). (3) De-risk the 'this is a property of GEPA plus one distiller prompt' reading by promoting the MIPROv2 optimizer arm and D_opt out of Tier 2 -- as written they are the last things run and the first things cut, yet prediction 9 and refutation (iii) both depend on them; a S_info that is reported for exactly one optimizer, one reflector (Claude) and one distiller prompt is a measurement of two prompts the authors wrote, and the two-bank-format check does not cover the instruction side. (4) Reconsider E1: BM25 multi-hop QA is a poor place to look for procedural experience value (the reusable lesson is roughly 'decompose and cite'), while E2/ALFWorld is the maximally template-repetitive case where a compiled block is nearly guaranteed to tie retrieval -- so prediction 4 is close to unfalsifiable there. A tool/web agent with recurring multi-step subroutines would make both the substitution and the compilation claims risky rather than pre-loaded. Separately, open the EvoAgentBench PDF before the design freeze, as promised.
reviews.missing_baseline: I1_{a+b}: a GEPA-optimized instruction trained on the union of both halves (all 800 episodes), evaluated with M0 and token-matched. The grid has I1a, I1b, I2a, I0, I_H, I3 and C_a but no instruction that was given the whole training set, even though that is the practitioner's actual alternative to a memory bank and the direct competitor to the paper's own deployment recommendation (cell 18, I1b x C_a). Without it the paper cannot answer the first question a reviewer will ask -- 'if I just run the optimizer on everything, do I need the bank at all?' -- and the compiled-block recommendation is compared only against instructions that each saw half the data, which structurally flatters C_a. Cost is small: one extra optimizer run set plus one 1000-instance cell, roughly 4 x 350 rollouts + 4,000 episodes, well under the Tier 2 budget already allocated to the gpt-oss-120b scale check. Second-order but also demandable: D_opt (the optimized static demonstration container) sits at Tier 2 and is fourth from the end of the cut order, yet refutation (iii) and any claim that 'compiled prose beats retrieval' explicitly require it -- a compile-wins result with D_opt unrun is exactly the 'prose beats exemplars' confound the authors say they want to exclude.
reviews.preprint_collision: Unusually strong in form, incomplete in exactly the place that matters. Credit where due: the check is dated (2026-09-03, prior scan 2026-08-21), reports its channels and volumes (15 HuggingFace queries, 244 papers, by-id verification of 54 arXiv IDs, targeted web search), commits raw scan records, names the closest work, explicitly withdraws a novelty sentence from v2 ('no published work uses one as the control for the other'), reinstates five citations v2 wrongly retracted, and states a procedural rule for future retractions. That is far above the median submission and is the opposite of an unsearched novelty claim. The weakness is that the single paper the entire novelty delta rests on was never actually read: arXiv is unreachable from the node, so EvoAgentBench's (2607.05202) absence claim -- no combined optimizer-plus-memory cell, no token matching, no paired statistics -- is inferred from an abstract, a project-page method list and search-surfaced descriptions of Table 3. Absence claims are the one kind of claim an abstract cannot support, and a combined GEPA-plus-bank cell is precisely the kind of thing that lives in an appendix or a robustness table. The same gap applies to 2608.14036's appendix, which the authors also flag. The residual-risk paragraph is honest (NeurIPS 2026 camera-readies in October; ICLR 2027 submissions not yet public; a 'GEPA + memory' ablation may exist in a systems-paper appendix) but does not discharge the problem. I also cannot independently verify any of the 2026-2027 identifiers cited here from my own knowledge, so my assessment of collision risk is conditional on the proposal's own reporting. Net: not a thin or vague check, and not a neutral either -- the novelty argument is currently load-bearing on an unopened PDF, and a reviewer is entitled to treat the delta as unestablished until that check is done.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A crossover identification for agentic memory: at a fixed GEPA-optimized instruction and on the same test instances, compare the gain of the bank distilled from the episodes that instruction was optimized on (own) against the gain of a bank from episodes it never saw (other), so that headroom is held constant by construction and the own-vs-other difference (Delta_info) isolates how much of memory's value is information the instruction container already absorbed. The design, not a method, is the contribution.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two threats, one conceded and one structural. (1) MIPROv2 (2406.11695) already factorizes a prompt into instructions plus bootstrapped demonstrations and reports instruction-only vs demonstration-only ablations on one training set - that IS the two-container question, and its recurring finding is that the split is task-dependent, which is close to what this proposal expects to find. It does not retrieve per query, does not distill, does not hold episodes out across containers, and reports no residual, so the crossover survives it. (2) EvoAgentBench (2607.05202, as the proposal describes it) puts Memento, ReasoningBank and GEPA on shared 528/267 trajectories across four domains and three backbones and already reports that GEPA nearly matches a curated reference on one backbone - which kills the 'nobody has compared them' framing (the proposal withdraws that sentence, correctly). The remaining delta is genuinely narrow: combined cells, token matching, the compiled arm, and the crossover. Note that I can verify the pre-2026 IDs cited here (2308.10144 ExpeL, 2406.11695 MIPROv2, 2507.19457 GEPA, 2509.25140 ReasoningBank, 2502.12110 A-MEM) and they are accurate, but every 26xx ID is past my own knowledge and I am taking the proposal's characterization of them on trust. Also close in shape: Experience Distillation (2607.21051), whose 'retains >=64.8% of the in-context gain' is the same retention-ratio object with weights as the second container - if that paper's method section contains a prompt-container arm, the novelty of the ratio itself is gone and only the own/other crossover remains.
reviews.strongest_objection: The primary endpoint is a ratio of two small, noisy quantities measured in the single cell hand-picked to make them as large as possible, and the headline generalizes from that cell to a whole literature. Concretely: A1 is the argmax over four agent x format pairings of the paired memory gain on S_dev at n=300, where the proposal itself states SE ~= 2.4pt. Selecting the maximum of four such draws under a >=6pt gate guarantees winner's-curse inflation of roughly 1.5-2pt, so the anchor gain g(I0,B_a) that looked like 7pt on S_dev plausibly regresses to 4-5pt on S_test. In that regime cells 6/7 and 9/10 give own ~1-2pt and other ~3-4pt, S_info = 1 - own/other carries a delta-method SE near 0.2, and the proposal's own rule declares S_info undefined whenever mean(other) < 3pt. The primary result can therefore be undefined or uninterpretable even when the hypothesis is true, and Prediction 1's conjunction (Delta_info >= 3pt AND S_info >= 0.5 with 90% CI excluding 0.2) survives only in a narrow window - roughly own <= 1-2pt with other >= 4pt at an optimized instruction. Risk 8 answers only half of this: it is right that S_info does not use the I0 denominator and so is not directly inflated by selection, but selection still determines whether there is any effect left to decompose. Second half of the objection: the paper is titled as a claim about the field ('Is Your Agent's Memory Just an Un-Optimized Prompt?') while Risk 11 explicitly refuses to re-measure any published number, and the robustness across agents is Qwen3.5-27B vs Qwen3-32B - two checkpoints of one vendor's family, with the only cross-family point (gpt-oss-120b, cell 25) declared out-of-scope, Tier 2, and first on the contingency cut list. The track brief demands that a methods contribution 'overturn or qualify specific existing results'; this qualifies an evaluation template using its own reimplementation on its own benchmark in its own most-favorable cell. Third, smaller but real: Delta_info > 0 does not distinguish substitution (the instruction already carries the lesson, so own-bank items add nothing) from interference (own-bank items duplicate and collide with an instruction tuned on the same episodes, which the track's own documented context-competition and dilution result makes likely). Those two mechanisms license opposite headlines and the moderator regression on similarity cannot separate them.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: 1) Pre-register the fix/break signature as a discriminating prediction, not a per-cell footnote: pure substitution predicts own has fewer FIXES than other at equal breaks; interference predicts own has more BREAKS. The instrumentation already logs this; make it Prediction 1b so the paper can name the mechanism instead of the ratio. 2) Promote the joint instruction+demonstration optimizer to Tier 0 (see missing_baseline) and add I1_ab, an instruction optimized on both halves (800 episodes), so the deployment question is answered at full data rather than only at half data. 3) Fix E2. The proposal states a treatment-free floor of 2.8-3.4pt at n=500; at ALFWorld's n=274 that floor scales to ~3.8-4.6pt, which exceeds the 3pt claim threshold and swamps the +/-4 TOST margin. Prediction 4's 'on E1 and E2' is therefore unsupportable as written; either raise E2's seeds and episode count until its floor is under 3pt, or state every E2 result as explicitly directional and stop citing it as replication. 4) Give the memory side a real equal-compute counterpart. B_tuned searches k in {3,5,7} plus a dedup threshold under a 350-rollout budget; that is hyperparameter selection, not a reflective improvement loop comparable to GEPA's, so outcome (viii) is not actually protected against. Add an iteratively re-distilled bank at matched rollouts and move the iso-cost arm off the Tier-2 cut list, since 'the second container is cheaper to serve' is doing rhetorical work the design currently checks only descriptively. 5) Retitle and rescope to what the design delivers: a substitution measurement for one screened agent x bank pairing in tool-augmented multi-hop QA, with the memory-null pairings reported as co-equal results rather than as an appendix. 6) Read the EvoAgentBench PDF before the design freeze, as already flagged - the entire remaining novelty claim is an absence claim about a paper nobody on the team has opened.
reviews.missing_baseline: The jointly optimized prompt - instructions AND demonstrations optimized together on the same training episodes, i.e. MIPROv2 in its actual published configuration or GEPA with the demonstration slot enabled. Every I1 arm here optimizes the instruction slot only, with memory absent from context, and the optimized-demonstration container appears solely as D_opt in cell 22: Tier 2, n=500, 1-2 seeds, first-block on the contingency cut list. This is the alternative a practitioner actually deploys and the true ceiling of the 'instruction container' argument. Without it the paper cannot answer the question it poses - if a jointly optimized prompt already matches I1b x C_a and I1a x M_a, then both the substitution finding and the 'compile once, do not retrieve' recommendation in cell 18 are moot, and a reviewer will say the study compared memory against a deliberately handicapped optimizer. Secondary omissions a reviewer will also raise: an instruction optimized on the union of both halves (I1_ab), absent entirely; and a matched-token, matched-decode compute control (e.g. self-consistency at the injected-token budget) to rule out 'any extra context/compute helps' - I3 pads tokens but adds no reasoning compute.
reviews.preprint_collision: Much better than the field norm in process, but its load-bearing conclusion is unverified. The good: dated scans (2026-08-21 and 2026-09-03), 15 named HuggingFace queries over 244 papers, by-id abstract verification for 54 IDs, committed scan records, and an honest correction of v2's false retraction of five citations that turned out to exist. The proposal also concedes the collision that matters - EvoAgentBench (2607.05202) already ran Memento, ReasoningBank and GEPA on shared trajectories, and the sentence claiming no such comparison exists is withdrawn. That concession is what a real check looks like. The defect: arXiv is unreachable from the node, EvoAgentBench's PDF was never opened, and the entire surviving novelty delta is stated as an ABSENCE claim about that paper's contents (no combined optimizer-plus-memory cell, no token matching, no paired statistics) resting on an abstract, a project-page method list, and search-surfaced descriptions of its Table 3. If that paper's appendix contains a +GEPA+RB combined cell - an ordinary thing for a benchmark paper with five methods and a shared split to include - the combined-cell claim collapses and only the own-vs-other crossover is left. The v2 episode cuts both ways: a search channel that produced five false negatives in August is not a channel that can certify a negative in September. Separately, the compiled-arm prediction is conceded to be directionally pre-empted (2608.14036 skills > Workflow Memory by 6.06pt; 2606.30775 single rewrite ~= iterative refinement), which is handled honestly by restating Prediction 4 as a quantified equivalence rather than a surprise. Net: the check is diligent and self-critical, and I am scoring it as a strength of the submission, but it does not yet establish novelty - the PDF check the proposal itself defers to the PI is a precondition for the novelty claim, not a nicety, and until it happens the residual risk named in the proposal (a 'GEPA + memory' ablation in some systems paper's appendix) is exactly the risk that would reduce this to a design-refinement paper.
